label: paragraph_title
text: KING AND QUEEN.

label: paragraph_title
text: INAUGURATE NEW GAS-WORKS PLANT.

label: text
text: LARGEST IN EUROPE.

label: text
text: Their Majesties the King and Queen were most warmly welcomed by the people of East London yesterday when they paid a visit to the gas-works at East Ham to in-nugurate the new inloading plant, which is the largest in Europe.

label: text
text: The King set in motion the new plant, and its method of handling coal was explained to His Majesty. It is capable of unloading by means of travelling cranes 2,000 tons of coal per hour. In order to carry the weight of new cranes, each weighing 120 tons, caissons were sunk into the river bed. The first unloading from the ebal steamer cranes delivers the fuel into small hoppers, and thence into two belt conveyors, the coal being automatically weighed in transit. The coal is then distributed to retort houses by aid of an elaborate railway system, which covers over 60 miles, of track--British Wireless Service.

label: paragraph_title
text: PRESIDENT'S FATE.

label: paragraph_title
text:
PRISONER IN FORTRESS
NEAR LISBON.

label: paragraph_title
text: Libson, July 10

label: text
text: The new Government being available to obtain from General Dr. Festa the transition of his powers as President, have resolved to imprison him in a fortress near Lisbon.

label: text
text: "His Aide de Campes are in custody on board a warship.-- Reuter.

label: paragraph_title
text: Liberated!

label: text
text: General D. Costa has been liberated and will be given a confidential mission abroad.—Reuter. For the Azores.

label: text
text: General Da Costa has embarked on a warship for the Azores. Reuter.

label: paragraph_title
text: TUBE STRIKE

label: paragraph_title
text: POWER HOUSE MEN JOIN

label: text
text: AMPLE CURRENT.

label: text
text:
New York, July 10.
The striking subway workers are now supported by one-third of the power house men, who struck this morning.

label: text
text: The current service, however, is being maintained.—Reuter's American Service.

label: paragraph_title
text: SÁSEBO PHOTÓS.

label: text
text:
OFFENCE BY U.S. CONSULAR
CLERK.

label: text
text: SECRET TRIAL.

label: text
text: The American Consular clerk, Vogelweid, who is charged with photographing, the Sasebo fortifications, underwent a secret preliminary trial in Nagasaki on Wednesday.

label: text
text: The case was adjourned till Monday, accused being remanded in custody of the Consul.—Reuter.

label: paragraph_title
text: FLOWING GOLD.

label: paragraph_title
text:
NEW YORK LOAN FOR
COLUMBIA?

label: text
text:
Bogota (Colombia), July 10.
The arrival of an official of the New York National City Bank has given rise to a report that a substantial loan is being made to the Government after the inauguration of the new President. The money will probably be used to finance public works and railways. Reuter.

label: paragraph_title
text: HEAT WAVE.

label: paragraph_title
text: DOZEN DEATHS IN NEW YORK.

label: text
text: The sweltering heat-wave continues. Thousands are sleeping in the open air. Hitherto, a dozen deaths have occurred and many prostrations. In the city eleven deaths have taken place, the others being on the Eastern seaboard. Reuter's American Service.

label: paragraph_title
text: OIL FIND.

label: text
text:
Paris, July 10.
The Matin announces that petroleum bearing land has been detected in Martinico.—Havas.

label: text
text: Fatalities are reported by two steamer which arrived in Hongkong during the week-end. From Calcutta and Singapore, the Hosang states: 2 males dead. The Van Overstratton, from Dell and Singapore, reports: One death, buried at sea. Both vessels are engaged in the trade which carried the emigrant class of passenger.

label: paragraph_title
text: TACNA-ARICA.

label: text
text: TO BE HANDED OVER TO BOLIVIA.

label: text
text: HOW PERU AND CHILE FARE.

label: text
text: New York, July 10.

label: text
text: It is reported from Santiago that negotiations are proceeding with Bolivia providing for handling over both Taena and Arica to Bolivia with compensation to Peru and Chile by Bolivia.—Reuter.

label: paragraph_title
text: COAL CRISIS.

label: text
text: NOTHING NEW EXPECTED FOR SOME TIME.

label: text
text: Although arrangements are complete for taking back to work the miners who present themselves in response to the colliery owners now wages offers, it is not expected that the full effect of the passage of the Eight Hour Bill, "which makes these offers possible, will be apparent immediately.

label: text
text: In Parliamentary circles the view is taken that any new move towards negotiations in the dispute is unlikely during the next few days, and that a week or a fortnight may elapse before any important development is recorded.

label: text
text: The safety men have continued in, the mines throughout the divide and it is reported that the pits have in consequence been kept in wood order in readiness for the men to start again.

label: text
text: The National Union of Railwaymen's delegate conference at Weymouth to-day decided to endorse the Executive's decision to take no action on the miners' request to impose an embargo on imported coal.—British Wireless Service.

label: paragraph_title
text: COBHAM'S FLIGHT.

label: text
text: NEW MECHANIC ACCEPTS

label: text
text: OFFERS

label: text
text: Mr. W. Moore has accepted the offer of the De Haviland Aircraft Company to take the place of Elliott, the mechanic of Alan Cobham's flight to Australia, who was killed by an Arab sniper's bullet.

label: text
text: Noore is an expert on air-cooled engines and is the chief tester at Coventry of the Armstrong-Sideley Jaguar engines with which Cobham's seaplane is fitted. He took part in the King's Cup Race three years ago, with Captain Courtney, who on that occasion won.—British Wireless Service.

label: paragraph_title
text: Cobham Proceeding.

label: text
text: Mr. Alan Cobham will leave on Tuesday accompanied by an Air Force mechanic, Sergeant Ward, without "waiting for the mechanic whom the De Havilland Company are sending out." Reuter.

label: paragraph_title
text: IN MORROCO.

label: paragraph_title
text: OPERATIONS IN THE TAZA AREA.

label: text
text: Rubat, July 10.

label: text
text:
General Boichut, who vanquished the Riffians, has departed to lead imminent operations against the Taza area, the last den of the mountain tribe who are still resisting.
According to the Petit Parisien five columns will participate in the operations.—Havns.

label: text
text: Sultan In France.

label: text
text: The Sultan of Morocco has arrived on board the cruiser Paris is order to attend the inauguration of the new Moslem Mosque in Paris and other ceremonies celebrating the victory over Abd-el-Krim.

label: text
text: " The cruiser received a salute of 21 guns.

label: text
text: Representatives of M. Doumergue and M. Briand boarded the cruiser and welcomed the Sultan.—Reuter.

label: paragraph_title
text: A "DREAM?"

label: paragraph_title
text: NEW USE FOR TROPICAL WEEDS.

label: text
text: London, July

label: text
text: Far reaching claims are made by an Indian doctor named Nanji, of Birmingham University, and Doctor Patron of Bristol University, for the new process of making natural vegetable fibres more useful to textile manufacturers. It is claimed to make fibre suitable for the existing spinning and weaving machinery from tropical growths hitherto considered rank weeds.

label: text
text: If this dream is fulfilled the whole textile industry might be revolutionised, and made more prosperous.—Reuter.

label: paragraph_title
text: KING'S CUP.

label: paragraph_title
text: ROUND BRITAIN, 2-DAYS AIR RACE.

label: text
text: WONDERFUL FEATS

label: text
text: Captain Broad, piloting a tiny Moth machine, was the winner of the King's Cup, in the two days' 1,464 miles air race, which ended last night.

label: text
text: The finish was sensationally close, the race being won from Flight Lt. Schofield, piloting a high-powered Vickers Yixen, by a margin of only 22 seconds.

label: text
text: Schofield, who, of course, conceded Broad a long start, averaged a speed of 140.2 miles hourly.

label: text
text: Only 5 of the original 14 entrants finished.

label: text
text: One of these was Squadron Leader Jones who came in third and won the prize for the fastest time in the race, with an average speed of 151.92 miles. — British Wireless Service.

label: text
text: Captain: Broad flew a 300 h.p. De Havilland Moth.

label: text
text: All-British machines were used, "with hardicap conditions ranging from an allowance of nearly five hours down to scratch.

label: text
text: The competitors made four circuits on two triangular courses, starting and finishing at Hendon, with engines ranging from 450 h.p. to 300 h.p.

label: text
text: Owing "to" various causes, only seven remained to start this morning. "Two" fell out of the course to-day.

label: text
text: Schofield used a 450 h.p. Vixen Napier.—Reuter.

label: paragraph_title
text: BRITAIN WINS AT TENNIS.

label: text
text: In the Davis Cup semi-final round (European zone of the lawn tennis international competition), Great Britain beat Spain by winning the first two singles and the doubles.

label: text
text: G. R. O. Crole Rees and C. H. Kingsley beat E. Flaquer and Morales 11-9, 6-4, 6-2.—Reuter.

label: text
text: In an earlier cable, it was stated that J. C. Gregory and Kingsley had each won a singles match.

label: paragraph_title
text: 24-HOUR CAR RECORD.

label: paragraph_title
text: Paris, July 11.

label: text
text: A 40 h.p.' car, driven alternatively by the drivers, is claimed to have broken the world's 24 hour record on the Linasmonth-lery track, covering 4,167 kilometres 578 metres. It is stated the previous record was 3,670 kilometres 829 metres.—Reuter.

label: text
text:
SUBMARINE S51 CREW AS
HEROES:

label: text
text: President Coolidge, in a statement, said that he was informed that when the hull of the S51 was explored, it was found that every man had died at his post, doing what he could to save the ship. The President paid a tribute and said the men could not have been greater heroes if they had died in action.—Reuter's American Service.

label: text
text: Eighteen of the bodies, of which six have not been identified, have now been removed from submarine S.51. They were placed in steel caskets and taken to the mortuary.

label: text
text: Three bereaved families were not allowed to see the bodies, which were identified by means of rings, teeth, and tattoo-marks.

label: text
text: Mr. Curtis D. Wilbur, Secretary of the Navy, personally congratulated the personnel of the salvage crew.—Reuter.

label: text
text: Earlier messages stuted: The removal of the bodies of the men trapped in Eubmarine S.51 began at the Brooklyn Navy Yard. The bodies were carried to the Navy Hospital, where the identification process is carried out by a fingerprint expert. The body of Lieut. Foster was first identified. Eight bodies have been recovered, and four more are known to be in the wreckage, whilst the torpedo-room has not yet been entered.

label: paragraph_title
text: CHO'LERA

label: paragraph_title
text: EUROPEAN LADY DIES IN SINGAPORE.

label: text
text:
[From Our Own Correspondent.]
Sinoanora Saturday

label: text
text: The steamer Erinpura, on which three cases of cholera occurred, has been disinfected and sailed for Rangoon.

label: text
text: Mrs. Hamilton, wife of Mr. A. W. B. Hamilton, who got cholera on the s.s. Erinpura, died to-day.

label: paragraph_title
text: SUNDAY MATCH.

label: paragraph_title
text: South China v. Filipinos.

label: text
text: The second meeting in the league between South China and the Philippines yesterday afternoon was even more closely contested than the first and the latter were again beaten by five runs to one.

label: text
text: It was thought that the Filipinos would pull the game through with the excellent fielding which they put up during the first six innings

label: text
text: when South China led by one run, but they fell off in the last inning with careless throws and allowed the Chinese to add three valuable runs. The mistakes were mostly at second and third base. Rull, at centre field, took three good catches which assisted in dismissing the South China men quickly.

label: text
text: The big hit of the afternoon was one to centre field by Zafra for a three-bagger. This brought Leonard home from second base to give the Filipinos their only run at the start. Run getters for South China were T. Chinn, June (2), K. Chinn and Sling.
